records.source: מַשָּׂ֖א צֹ֑ר הֵילִ֣ילוּ׀אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֗ישׁ כִּֽי־שֻׁדַּ֤ד מִבַּ֨יִת֙ מִבּ֔וֹא מֵאֶ֥רֶץ כִּתִּ֖ים נִגְלָה־לָֽמוֹ׃
records.gloss: [The] oracle [of] Tyre. Wail, ships of Tarshish, for it has been devastated, from house, from coming in; from [the] land of Kittim it has been revealed to them.
pieces: The oracle concerning Tyre. \q Wail, ships of Tarshish! Tyre lies in ruins, with no house left standing and no port to come home to. \q From the land of Kittim the news has reached them.

L.1: The oracle of Tyre. \q Wail, ships of Tarshish, for it is devastated, without house, without entering; \q from the land of Kittim it has been revealed to them.

R.1: This is a message about Tyre. \q Cry out in grief, you sailors on the great trading ships! Tyre has been destroyed. No houses are left, and there is no harbor where your ships can come home. \q You heard the news on the way home, in Cyprus.

decisions.choice: oracle: a weighty message from God
decisions.reason: The word heads the oracles against the nations (see the note at 13:1). This one concerns Tyre, the great Phoenician port on an island off the coast, and its sister city Sidon (verses 2, 4, 12).

decisions.choice: ships of Tarshish: large seagoing trading ships
decisions.reason: Tarshish was a distant port far to the west (Jonah 1:3); its name was given to the large ships that made such long voyages (2:16; 1 Kings 10:22). The poem opens and closes with these ships (verse 14).

decisions.choice: without house, without entering: Tyre is left with no home and no harbor; the sailors learn it at Kittim
alternatives: destroyed, so that no one can enter from home
decisions.reason: The two short phrases say Tyre is destroyed so that there is no house and no way in. Kittim is Cyprus (its city Kition), the last stop for ships sailing home to Tyre from the west.

decisions.choice: message
decisions.reason: Readable says "message" for "oracle", as at 13:1.

decisions.choice: great trading ships
decisions.reason: Readable says what ships of Tarshish were: large ships built for long trading voyages (2:16). Readable speaks to the sailors on them.

decisions.choice: Tyre / no port to come home to; Cyprus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Tyre as the city destroyed and say what "without entering" means for ships. Readable says "Cyprus" for Kittim.

records.heading: The oracle concerning Tyre

records.source: דֹּ֖מּוּ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי אִ֑י סֹחֵ֥ר צִיד֛וֹן עֹבֵ֥ר יָ֖ם מִלְאֽוּךְ׃
records.gloss: Be silent, inhabitants of [the] coastland, merchant of Sidon, passing over [the] sea, they have filled you.
pieces: Be still, you people of the coast, \q whom Sidon's traders filled with wealth as they sailed the sea.

L.2: Be silent, inhabitants of the coastland! \q The merchants of Sidon, crossing [the] sea, filled you.

R.2: Be quiet, you people who live on the coast. \q Traders from Sidon sailed across the sea and made you rich.

decisions.choice: be silent: be stunned into silence, as mourners are
decisions.reason: The verb means to be still or silent; here it is the silence of shock and grief (compare Lamentations 2:10).

decisions.choice: the merchant of Sidon: the merchants as a group, who filled the coast with goods and wealth
decisions.reason: The word is singular but the verb "they filled" is plural, so the merchant stands for all of Sidon's traders. The coastland is the Phoenician coast of Tyre and Sidon.

decisions.choice: crossing the sea, they filled you: the traditional Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) reads "they crossed the sea, your messengers", joining the words to the start of verse 3. The traditional text gives good sense and is followed here; reviewers should check the scroll's wording.

decisions.choice: filled with wealth / made you rich
decisions.reason: "Filled you" means filled with goods and riches; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וּבְמַ֤יִם רַבִּים֙ זֶ֣רַע שִׁחֹ֔ר קְצִ֥יר יְא֖וֹר תְּבֽוּאָתָ֑הּ וַתְּהִ֖י סְחַ֥ר גּוֹיִֽם׃
records.gloss: And on many waters [was] [the] seed of Shihor, [the] harvest of [the] Nile [was] her revenue; and she became [the] market of nations.
pieces: The grain of Shihor crossed the mighty waters; \q what the Nile harvested brought her income, \q and she grew into a market for the nations.

L.3: And on many waters [came] the grain of Shihor; \q the harvest of the Nile [was] her revenue, \q and she became the market of nations.

R.3: Ships carried grain from Egypt across the sea. \q The crops that grew beside the Nile River made Tyre rich. \q She became the place where the nations came to buy and sell.

decisions.choice: Shihor and the Nile: the waters of Egypt and its grain
decisions.reason: Shihor is a water at the edge of Egypt, probably a branch of the Nile (Joshua 13:3; Jeremiah 2:18). Egypt's grain was carried by Phoenician ships, and Tyre grew rich on the trade.

decisions.choice: her: Tyre, the city addressed in the poem
decisions.reason: The feminine pronoun refers to the city. Cities are spoken of as women throughout the chapter (verses 7, 12, 15-17).

decisions.choice: Ships carried grain from Egypt / made Tyre rich
decisions.reason: Readable says that the grain came by ship from Egypt and names Tyre for "her".

records.source: בּ֣וֹשִׁי צִיד֔וֹן כִּֽי־אָמַ֣ר יָ֔ם מָע֥וֹז הַיָּ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹֽא־חַ֣לְתִּי וְלֹֽא־יָלַ֗דְתִּי וְלֹ֥א גִדַּ֛לְתִּי בַּחוּרִ֖ים רוֹמַ֥מְתִּי בְתוּלֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Be ashamed, Sidon, for has said [the] sea, [the] stronghold of the sea, saying, not I have been in labor and not I have given birth, and not I have brought up young men, I have raised young women.
pieces: Hang your head in shame, Sidon, \q because the sea, the sea's stronghold, cries out: \q "I have known no labor pains and borne no children; I have raised no young men and brought up no young women."

L.4: Be ashamed, Sidon, for the sea has spoken, \q the stronghold of the sea, saying, \q "I have not been in labor and I have not given birth, and I have not brought up young men, [nor] raised young women."

R.4: Sidon, be ashamed! \q The sea has spoken, the strong fortress out in the sea. It says, \q "I am like a woman who has no children. I never went through labor or gave birth. I never raised boys to be young men or girls to be young women."

decisions.choice: the sea, the stronghold of the sea: the sea speaks, and Tyre, its island fortress, speaks with it
alternatives: the sea, that is, Tyre the fortress of the sea
decisions.reason: The second phrase may name the sea again or name Tyre, the fortress set in the sea. Either way the voice is that of the sea and the city in it.

decisions.choice: I have not given birth: like a woman who has lost all her children
decisions.reason: The sea, which had been like a mother to the coastal cities, speaks as if she had never had children at all: her young people are gone. Sidon is shamed because the mother of her trade is left childless.

decisions.choice: I am like a woman who has no children
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture behind the sea's words.

records.gloss: When [the] report [comes] to Egypt, they will be in anguish like [at] the report of Tyre.
pieces: When the news reaches Egypt, \q they will shake with pain at what they hear of Tyre.

L.5: When the report [comes] to Egypt, \q they will writhe at the report of Tyre.

R.5: When the people of Egypt hear the news about Tyre, \q they will tremble with grief.

decisions.choice: when the report comes to Egypt, they will writhe at the report of Tyre
alternatives: as at the report about Egypt, so they will writhe at the report about Tyre
decisions.reason: The first word can mean "when" or "as". Read as "as", the line compares the two: as at the news about Egypt, so they will writhe at the news about Tyre. The reading "when" fits verse 3, where Egypt's grain trade depends on Tyre.

decisions.choice: be in anguish: writhe, as a woman in labor
decisions.reason: The verb describes twisting in pain, often of childbirth, and echoes the labor of verse 4.

records.gloss: Pass over to Tarshish; wail, inhabitants of [the] coastland.
pieces: Sail away to Tarshish! \q Wail, you who live on the coast!

L.6: Cross over to Tarshish; \q wail, inhabitants of the coastland!

R.6: Escape by ship to Tarshish, far to the west! \q Cry out in grief, you people who live on the coast!

decisions.choice: cross over to Tarshish: flee by sea to the far west
decisions.reason: Tarshish was the most distant western port the Phoenicians sailed to (Jonah 1:3). The people of the coast are told to flee there as refugees.

decisions.choice: Escape by ship ... far to the west
decisions.reason: Readable says why they cross the sea and where Tarshish lay.

records.source: הֲזֹ֥את לָכֶ֖ם עַלִּיזָ֑ה מִֽימֵי־קֶ֤דֶם קַדְמָתָהּ֙ יֹבִל֣וּהָ רַגְלֶ֔יהָ מֵֽרָח֖וֹק לָגֽוּר׃
records.gloss: [Is] this to you [the] exultant [one], from days of antiquity [is] her beginning? Have carried her her feet from afar to sojourn.
pieces: Is this your rejoicing city, \q whose story began in ancient days? Her own feet took her far away to make her home among strangers.

L.7: Is this your exultant [city], \q whose beginning [is] from days of old? Her feet carried her far away to sojourn.

R.7: Is this really your happy, noisy city? \q Tyre was founded long, long ago. Her own feet took her far away to live as a stranger.

decisions.choice: exultant: full of noisy joy and pride
decisions.reason: The word describes loud celebration, and in 22:2 and 32:13 a city given to revelry. The question mocks Tyre's old confidence.

decisions.choice: her feet carried her far away to sojourn: she went far off to live as a foreigner
alternatives: her people will be carried off to live in exile
decisions.reason: The line may look back on Tyre's traders who settled in colonies across the sea, or forward to her people driven into exile in foreign lands. The words allow both.

decisions.choice: Tyre was founded
decisions.reason: Readable names Tyre and says "founded" for "her beginning".

records.source: מִ֚י יָעַ֣ץ זֹ֔את עַל־צֹ֖ר הַמַּֽעֲטִירָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר סֹחֲרֶ֨יה֙ שָׂרִ֔ים כִּנְעָנֶ֖יהָ נִכְבַּדֵּי־אָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Who planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose traders [were] princes, her merchants [were] [the] honored of [the] earth?
pieces: Who made this plan against Tyre, which once handed out crowns? \q Her traders ranked as princes; \q her merchants were honored across the earth.

L.8: Who planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, \q whose traders [were] princes, \q her merchants the honored of the earth?

R.8: Who planned this disaster for Tyre? Tyre was the city that gave out crowns. \q Her traders lived like princes. \q People all over the world honored her merchants.

decisions.choice: the bestower of crowns: the city that set up kings
decisions.reason: Tyre made rulers in the colonies it founded. The form could also mean "the crowned city", the city wearing a crown.

decisions.choice: merchants: literally "her Canaanites"
decisions.reason: Because the Phoenicians, the people of Canaan's coast, were the great traders, "Canaanite" came to mean a merchant (Zephaniah 1:11; Proverbs 31:24).

decisions.choice: who planned this: a question answered in verse 9
decisions.reason: The question prepares for the answer that follows: the plan is God's.

records.source: יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת יְעָצָ֑הּ לְחַלֵּל֙ גְּא֣וֹן כָּל־צְבִ֔י לְהָקֵ֖ל כָּל־נִכְבַּדֵּי־אָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Yahweh of hosts planned it, to profane [the] pride of all splendor, to treat with contempt all [the] honored of [the] earth.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies planned it, \q to stain the pride that every splendor brings \q and to bring low all the earth's honored ones.

L.9: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts planned it, \q to defile the pride of all splendor, \q to treat as light all the honored of the earth.

R.9: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies planned it. \q He planned to take away the pride that people felt in their beauty and wealth. \q He planned to bring shame on all the famous people of the earth.

decisions.choice: to defile: to make common what was held high
decisions.reason: The verb means to profane or treat as common. God strips away the honor in which Tyre's glory was held.

decisions.choice: to treat as light the honored: a play on heavy and light
decisions.reason: "Honored" comes from the root "heavy" and "treat with contempt" from the root "light": the weighty people of the earth will count for nothing. The same pair answers the question of verse 8 (compare 2:12-17).

decisions.choice: beauty and wealth
decisions.reason: Readable says what Tyre's splendor was.

records.source: עִבְרִ֥י אַרְצֵ֖ךְ כַּיְאֹ֑ר בַּת־תַּרְשִׁ֕ישׁ אֵ֖ין מֵ֥זַח עֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: Pass over your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish; there is not a restraint any longer.
pieces: Spread over your land as the Nile spreads, \q Daughter Tarshish; nothing holds you in any longer.

L.10: Pass through your land like the Nile, \q daughter of Tarshish; [there is] no longer a restraint.

R.10: People of Tarshish, spread out over your land, as the Nile River floods over its banks. \q Nothing holds you back anymore.

decisions.choice: pass through: the traditional Hebrew text
alternatives: work your land like the Nile
decisions.reason: The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) reads "work your land", and the Septuagint has "work your land, for ships no longer come from Carthage". The traditional text is followed here: Tarshish may flow freely over its land like the Nile in flood.

decisions.choice: restraint: a belt or bond that holds something in
decisions.reason: The word is rare (Psalm 109:19 uses a related word for a belt). It most likely means that Tyre's hold over Tarshish is gone. A harbor or dock is another possible sense.

decisions.choice: People of Tarshish
decisions.reason: "Daughter Tarshish" pictures the people of the city as a young woman; Readable says "people of Tarshish".

records.source: יָדוֹ֙ נָטָ֣ה עַל־הַיָּ֔ם הִרְגִּ֖יז מַמְלָכ֑וֹת יְהוָה֙ צִוָּ֣ה אֶל־כְּנַ֔עַן לַשְׁמִ֖ד מָעֻזְנֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: His hand he has stretched out over the sea; he has made tremble kingdoms. Yahweh has commanded concerning Canaan to destroy her strongholds.
pieces: He has reached out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand over the sea \q and set kingdoms trembling. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has issued orders against Canaan, \q that her fortresses be torn down.

L.11: His hand {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has stretched out over the sea; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made kingdoms tremble. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has given command concerning Canaan, \q to destroy her strongholds.

R.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand over the sea. \q He has made kingdoms shake with fear. \q He has given the order to destroy the fortresses of Canaan, the land of Tyre and Sidon.

decisions.choice: his hand stretched out over the sea: God's power over the sea
decisions.reason: The stretched-out hand is God's hand of judgment (5:25; 14:26-27). Over the sea, it recalls the crossing of the sea in Exodus 14:21.

decisions.choice: Canaan: the Phoenician coast
decisions.reason: Here Canaan means the coastland of Tyre and Sidon, the old name for the land of the Phoenicians (Genesis 10:15).

decisions.choice: the LORD as subject; the land of Tyre and Sidon
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD at the start and says which part of Canaan is meant.

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא־תוֹסִ֥יפִי ע֖וֹד לַעְל֑וֹז הַֽמְעֻשָּׁקָ֞ה בְּתוּלַ֣ת בַּת־צִיד֗וֹן כִּתִּים֙ ק֣וּמִי עֲבֹ֔רִי גַּם־שָׁ֖ם לֹא־יָנ֥וּחַֽ לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And he said, not you will again exult, O oppressed one, virgin daughter of Sidon; [to] Kittim arise, pass over; also there not it will be rest to you.
pieces: He said: You will celebrate no more, \q you ravaged virgin, Daughter Sidon. Get up, cross over to Kittim; \q even there no rest awaits you.

L.12: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said: You will not again exult, \q oppressed one, virgin daughter of Sidon! [To] Kittim, arise, cross over; \q even there [there] will be no rest for you.

R.12: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said this: People of Sidon, you will never celebrate again. \q You are like a young woman who has been crushed. Get up and escape by ship to Cyprus. \q But even there you will not find rest.

decisions.choice: he said: the LORD of verse 11
decisions.reason: The speaker is not named; the nearest is the LORD, who gave the command against Canaan in verse 11.

decisions.choice: oppressed virgin: a city never taken, now crushed and violated
decisions.reason: The city is pictured as a young woman. "Virgin" marks her as never conquered; the verb means crushed or wronged by force (compare 47:1).

decisions.choice: Kittim: Cyprus
decisions.reason: Refugees from Sidon would flee to Cyprus, where the Phoenicians had colonies (verse 1). The written text has a longer spelling of the same name; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: People of Sidon ... like a young woman who has been crushed
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, speaks to the people, and states the picture as a comparison.

records.source: הֵ֣ן׀אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים זֶ֤ה הָעָם֙ לֹ֣א הָיָ֔ה אַשּׁ֖וּר יְסָדָ֣הּ לְצִיִּ֑ים הֵקִ֣ימוּ בַחוּנָ֗יו עֹרְרוּ֙ אַרְמְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ שָׂמָ֖הּ לְמַפֵּלָֽה׃
records.gloss: Look, [the] land of [the] Chaldeans, this [is] the people [that] not was; Assyria assigned it to desert creatures. They raised up its siege towers, they laid bare its palaces, it made it into a ruin.
pieces: See the land of the Chaldeans, a people who no longer exist! \q Assyria gave it over to the beasts of the wilderness. \q Its siege towers went up, its palaces were torn bare, \q and it was left a heap of rubble.

L.13: Look, the land of the Chaldeans! This [is] the people [that] is no more; \q Assyria assigned it to desert creatures. \q They raised up its siege towers; they stripped its palaces; \q [one] made it a ruin.

R.13: Look at what happened to the land of Babylonia. Its people are gone. \q The Assyrians turned it into a place where only wild animals live. \q They built towers to attack the city. They tore down its palaces and left it in ruins.

decisions.choice: this is the people that is no more; Assyria assigned it
decisions.reason: The words may also be read "this is the people; it was not Assyria", setting the Chaldeans against Assyria. Read as here, the verse points to Babylon's ruin at Assyria's hands (Sennacherib destroyed Babylon in 689 BC): if Babylon could fall, so can Tyre.

decisions.choice: desert creatures: wild animals of the dry places
decisions.reason: The word means those who live in the desert, animals or nomads; it is used for wild creatures in ruins in 13:21 and 34:14.

decisions.choice: siege towers: towers built against a city's walls
decisions.reason: The word is rare; it names the towers an army raised to attack a city. The written text and the scribes' reading differ only in a vowel letter.

decisions.choice: Babylonia
decisions.reason: Readable says "Babylonia" for "the land of the Chaldeans", the people who lived in southern Babylonia.

records.source: הֵילִ֖ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ כִּ֥י שֻׁדַּ֖ד מָעֻזְּכֶֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Wail, ships of Tarshish, for has been devastated your stronghold.
pieces: Wail, ships of Tarshish, \q for your fortress has been laid waste!

L.14: Wail, ships of Tarshish, \q for your stronghold is devastated!

R.14: Cry out in grief, you sailors on the great trading ships! \q The strong city where you were safe has been destroyed.

decisions.choice: wail, ships of Tarshish: the poem ends as it began
decisions.reason: The cry repeats verse 1 and closes the poem; the stronghold is Tyre, the home port of the ships.

decisions.choice: great trading ships
decisions.reason: Readable says what ships of Tarshish were: large ships built for long trading voyages (2:16). Readable speaks to the sailors on them.

decisions.choice: the strong city where you were safe
decisions.reason: Readable says what the ships' stronghold was.

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְנִשְׁכַּ֤חַת צֹר֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה כִּימֵ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ אֶחָ֑ד מִקֵּ֞ץ שִׁבְעִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לְצֹ֔ר כְּשִׁירַ֖ת הַזּוֹנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it will be in the day the that, and [will be] forgotten Tyre seventy years like [the] days of a king one; from [the] end of seventy years it will be to Tyre like the song of the prostitute:
pieces: On that day Tyre will drop out of memory for seventy years, as long as one king's lifetime. At the close of those seventy years, Tyre's story will be like the prostitute's song:

L.15: And it will be in that day that Tyre will be forgotten seventy years, like the days of one king. At the end of seventy years it will be for Tyre like the song of the prostitute:

R.15: At that time people will forget about Tyre for seventy years. That is about as long as a king lives. After the seventy years, Tyre will be like the woman in this song about a prostitute:

decisions.choice: seventy years: a full lifetime of judgment
decisions.reason: Seventy years is a full human life (Psalm 90:10) and the length Jeremiah gives for the nations' service to Babylon (Jeremiah 25:11-12; 29:10).

decisions.choice: like the days of one king: the length of one reign or lifetime
alternatives: like the reign of one dynasty
decisions.reason: The phrase means a long but limited span: one king's reign, or a lifetime. It may also mean an unchanging time, as under a single king.

decisions.choice: the song of the prostitute: a popular song, quoted in verse 16
decisions.reason: The song mocks an aging prostitute who must sing in the streets to be noticed again. Trade for profit is pictured as prostitution, as with Nineveh in Nahum 3:4.

records.heading: Tyre forgotten for seventy years

records.source: קְחִ֥י כִנּ֛וֹר סֹ֥בִּי עִ֖יר זוֹנָ֣ה נִשְׁכָּחָ֑ה הֵיטִ֤יבִי נַגֵּן֙ הַרְבִּי־שִׁ֔יר לְמַ֖עַן תִּזָּכֵֽרִי׃
records.gloss: Take a harp, go around [the] city, O prostitute forgotten; do well playing, multiply song, so that you may be remembered.
pieces: "Pick up a harp and walk through the city, you prostitute whom everyone forgot! \q Play sweetly, sing song after song, \q so that someone will remember you."

L.16: "Take a harp, go around the city, forgotten prostitute! \q Play well, sing many songs, \q so that you may be remembered."

R.16: "You prostitute whom everyone has forgotten, take your harp and walk around the city. \q Play your music well. Sing many songs so that people will remember you."

decisions.choice: take a harp, go around: the words of the song
decisions.reason: The verse is the song named in verse 15. It speaks to the forgotten prostitute, a picture of Tyre after seventy years.

decisions.choice: harp: a stringed instrument held in the hands
decisions.reason: The word is the lyre played at feasts and in worship (5:12; Genesis 4:21).

records.source: וְהָיָ֞ה מִקֵּ֣ץ׀שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה יִפְקֹ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־צֹ֔ר וְשָׁבָ֖ה לְאֶתְנַנָּ֑ה וְזָֽנְתָ֛ה אֶת־כָּל־מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאָ֖רֶץ עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it will be from [the] end of seventy years, will visit Yahweh Tyre, and she will return to her hire and she will prostitute herself with all [the] kingdoms of the earth on [the] face of the ground.
pieces: At the end of the seventy years {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will turn {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} attention to Tyre. She will go back to earning her fee, selling herself to every kingdom of the world across the face of the earth.

L.17: And it will be at the end of seventy years [that] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will visit Tyre, and she will return to her wages and will play the prostitute with all the kingdoms of the earth on the face of the ground.

R.17: After seventy years, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will come to help Tyre again. Then she will go back to trading for profit, like a prostitute who sells herself for pay. She will do business with all the kingdoms of the world.

decisions.choice: visit: attend to, here to restore
decisions.reason: The verb means to give attention to someone, for judgment or for help. After the seventy years God attends to Tyre and allows her to rise again (compare Jeremiah 29:10).

decisions.choice: her wages, play the prostitute: trade for profit with the nations
decisions.reason: The picture of verse 15 continues. Tyre's trade with every kingdom is like a prostitute's dealings with her clients: done for pay, with no loyalty (compare Nahum 3:4; Ezekiel 27).

decisions.choice: trading for profit, like a prostitute
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means and keeps it as a comparison.

decisions.choice: turn his attention to / come to help
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "visit"; Balanced and Readable say what the visit means here.

records.source: וְהָיָ֨ה סַחְרָ֜הּ וְאֶתְנַנָּ֗הּ קֹ֚דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֔ה לֹ֥א יֵֽאָצֵ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יֵֽחָסֵ֑ן כִּ֣י לַיֹּשְׁבִ֞ים לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה סַחְרָ֔הּ לֶאֱכֹ֥ל לְשָׂבְעָ֖ה וְלִמְכַסֶּ֥ה עָתִֽיק׃פ
records.gloss: And will be her trading profit and her hire a holy thing to Yahweh; not it will be stored up and not it will be hoarded, for to those dwelling before Yahweh will belong her trading profit, for eating to satiety and for covering magnificent.
pieces: Yet what she gains and what she is paid will be holy, belonging to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. No one will lock it away or pile it up. Her earnings will go to those who live in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to give them all the food they want and splendid clothing.

L.18: And her profit and her wages will be holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; it will not be stored up and will not be hoarded, for her profit will belong to those who dwell before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for eating to the full and for splendid covering.

R.18: But the money Tyre earns will be given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It will be holy. No one will save it up or keep it for themselves. It will go to the people who live in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They will have plenty to eat and fine clothes to wear.

decisions.choice: holy to the LORD: set apart for God
decisions.reason: Tyre's earnings, once the wages of her trade, will be dedicated to God. The nations' wealth comes to God's people again in 60:5-11 and 61:6.

decisions.choice: those who dwell before the LORD: those who serve in God's presence
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean the priests and worshipers at the temple, or more widely God's people who live before him.

decisions.choice: splendid covering: fine clothing
decisions.reason: The covering is clothing; the rare adjective means choice or magnificent.
